    "argument_markdown": "## Source-backed inputs\n\nATT-0065, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109, supplies the canonical balanced filtration without a global splitting and the intrinsic scheme-theoretic Fitting/Picard identity. ATT-0066, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, supplies the closed Abel\u2013Jacobi incidence, its reduced constant-h\u2070 projective-bundle model, and the scheme-theoretic ordered/unordered comparison on Conf\u2086. SRC-0004 fixes the essential convention W_f=(O(2)\u2297\u03b3*O(-f))|_C. FND-0105 is retained as the explicit normalization hypothesis. FND-0125 supplies the normalization-free exclusion of hyperelliptic-composed covers from the balanced splitting, and FND-0130 supplies the plane-quintic CE exclusion used below.\n\n## Proved steps\n\n1. Write O_C(D)=\u03b3*O(1). Hypothesis (N) gives O(1)|_C\u2245\u03c9_{C/S}\u2297\u03b3*O(2); therefore W_5\u2245\u03c9_{C/S}^{\u22972}(-D) and L\u2245\u03c9_{C/S}(-D). On a geometric fibre, O(D) has degree four and at least two sections. Clifford gives h\u2070(O(D))\u22643. Equality would be Clifford equality, so C would be hyperelliptic and every pencil in |D| would factor as \u03b3=q\u2218h. FND-0125 then gives relations splitting O(2)\u2295O(7), contradicting O(4)\u2295O(5). Thus h\u2070(O(D))=2. Riemann\u2013Roch and Serre duality now give h\u00b9(L)=2 and h\u2070(L)=1+h\u00b9(L)=3. In particular the h\u2070=4 branch is empty.\n\n2. Since S is reduced and both fibre dimensions are constant, Grauert gives \u03c0_*L locally free of rank three, R\u00b9\u03c0_*L locally free of rank two, and base change. ATT-0066 identifies the closed Abel\u2013Jacobi incidence canonically with I\u2245P_S((\u03c0_*L)^\u2228). Hence I\u2192S is a Zariski-locally trivial P\u00b2-bundle, smooth and proper of pure relative dimension two.\n\n3. The bundle L is base-point-free. Indeed, a base point p would make L(-p) a g\u00b2_5. The genus-six classification used in FND-0130 forces the smooth plane-quintic case; because L=\u03c9(-D), the given tetragonal pencil is projection from p. The CE restriction calculation in FND-0130 makes that projection splitting unbalanced, contradicting (BAL). Thus |L_s| is base-point-free on every geometric fibre. In characteristic zero its associated morphism to P\u00b2 is separable, so Bertini gives a reduced general hyperplane pullback. Consequently V_s is a nonempty dense open of |L_s|\u2245P\u00b2 for every s. This uses base-point-freeness and Bertini, not \u03c7(L)=1.\n\n4. ATT-0066 identifies the pullback of I to Conf\u2086 with Z_ev as an equality of ideals, not merely of geometric points. Because Conf\u2086 already imposes distinct support, this pullback is the ordered incidence over V. Ordering six distinct points gives a finite \u00e9tale S\u2086-torsor Z_ev\u2192V. The deck action is free: a permutation fixing an ordered tuple of six pairwise-distinct points is the identity. This statement concerns the deck group only and says nothing about automorphisms of the marked curve.\n\n5. The open V is S-smooth of pure relative dimension two, and finite \u00e9tale pullback shows that Z_ev is S-smooth of pure relative dimension two. Conf\u2086(C/S) is S-smooth of relative dimension six. Since the Abel\u2013Jacobi/Fitting identity makes Z_ev closed in Conf\u2086, a closed immersion between S-smooth schemes is regular. The relative dimension difference is four, so the conormal is locally free of rank four; the conormal sequence splits locally because \u03a9_{Z_ev/S} is locally free. This lci conclusion comes from relative smoothness, not from determinantal expected codimension.\n\n6. For each irreducible component S_\u03b1, the projective bundle I_\u03b1 is irreducible, and V_\u03b1=V\u2229I_\u03b1 is nonempty open and hence irreducible and dense. Thus components of I and V correspond to those of S and have dimension dim(S_\u03b1)+2 when finite-dimensional. For a component T of Z_ev, flatness of the finite \u00e9tale map makes the contraction of its generic point a generic point of V; finiteness then makes T\u2192V_\u03b1 surjective. Hence dim(T)=dim(V_\u03b1)=dim(S_\u03b1)+2. The number of such T over V_\u03b1 is not determined without additional normality and monodromy input.\n\n## Computational hypotheses\n\nNone. No finite experiment is used to establish a universal claim.\n\n## Remaining scope\n\nThe proof is relative over a reduced scheme base. It does not descend the projective-bundle argument to a stack base, determine moduli inertia, or establish any closed embedding, absolute codimension, Gysin morphism, or Tate statement in M_{6,6}.",

    "theorem_statement": "Let k be a characteristic-zero field and S a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme. Let \u03c0:C\u2192S be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected genus-six curves equipped with a finite flat degree-four map \u03b3:C\u2192P\u00b9_S, the standard degree-four Casnati\u2013Ekedahl resolution, fibrewise balanced relations bundle F_s\u2245O(4)\u2295O(5), its canonical filtration with quotient W_5 of degree 16, and the weak relative-canonical normalization (N). Put L=W_5\u2297\u03c9_{C/S}^{-1}, let I=Hilb\u2076(C/S)\u00d7_{Pic\u2076(C/S)}S be the Abel\u2013Jacobi incidence over [L], let V=I^{dist} be its distinct-support open, and let Z_ev\u2282Conf\u2086(C/S) be the intrinsic evaluation-failure scheme. Then every geometric fibre has h\u2070(L_s)=3 and h\u00b9(L_s)=2; I\u2245P_S((\u03c0_*L)^\u2228) is a P\u00b2-bundle; V is nonempty and dense in every fibre; and Z_ev is scheme-theoretically the ordered incidence over V. The morphism Z_ev\u2192V is a finite \u00e9tale S\u2086-torsor with free deck action, Z_ev\u2192S is smooth of pure relative dimension two, and Z_ev\u21aaConf\u2086(C/S) is a regular immersion of pure codimension four with locally free conormal of rank four. Irreducible components of I and V correspond to irreducible components of S; every irreducible component of Z_ev maps finitely and surjectively onto one component of V and, over a finite-dimensional component S_\u03b1, has dimension dim(S_\u03b1)+2. No count of the components of Z_ev is asserted."

parsed_artifact.argument_markdown:
## Source-backed inputs

ATT-0065, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109, supplies the canonical balanced filtration without a global splitting and the intrinsic scheme-theoretic Fitting/Picard identity. ATT-0066, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, supplies the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence, its reduced constant-h⁰ projective-bundle model, and the scheme-theoretic ordered/unordered comparison on Conf₆. SRC-0004 fixes the essential convention W_f=(O(2)⊗γ*O(-f))|_C. FND-0105 is retained as the explicit normalization hypothesis. FND-0125 supplies the normalization-free exclusion of hyperelliptic-composed covers from the balanced splitting, and FND-0130 supplies the plane-quintic CE exclusion used below.

## Proved steps

1. Write O_C(D)=γ*O(1). Hypothesis (N) gives O(1)|_C≅ω_{C/S}⊗γ*O(2); therefore W_5≅ω_{C/S}^{⊗2}(-D) and L≅ω_{C/S}(-D). On a geometric fibre, O(D) has degree four and at least two sections. Clifford gives h⁰(O(D))≤3. Equality would be Clifford equality, so C would be hyperelliptic and every pencil in |D| would factor as γ=q∘h. FND-0125 then gives relations splitting O(2)⊕O(7), contradicting O(4)⊕O(5). Thus h⁰(O(D))=2. Riemann–Roch and Serre duality now give h¹(L)=2 and h⁰(L)=1+h¹(L)=3. In particular the h⁰=4 branch is empty.

2. Since S is reduced and both fibre dimensions are constant, Grauert gives π_*L locally free of rank three, R¹π_*L locally free of rank two, and base change. ATT-0066 identifies the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence canonically with I≅P_S((π_*L)^∨). Hence I→S is a Zariski-locally trivial P²-bundle, smooth and proper of pure relative dimension two.

3. The bundle L is base-point-free. Indeed, a base point p would make L(-p) a g²_5. The genus-six classification used in FND-0130 forces the smooth plane-quintic case; because L=ω(-D), the given tetragonal pencil is projection from p. The CE restriction calculation in FND-0130 makes that projection splitting unbalanced, contradicting (BAL). Thus |L_s| is base-point-free on every geometric fibre. In characteristic zero its associated morphism to P² is separable, so Bertini gives a reduced general hyperplane pullback. Consequently V_s is a nonempty dense open of |L_s|≅P² for every s. This uses base-point-freeness and Bertini, not χ(L)=1.

4. ATT-0066 identifies the pullback of I to Conf₆ with Z_ev as an equality of ideals, not merely of geometric points. Because Conf₆ already imposes distinct support, this pullback is the ordered incidence over V. Ordering six distinct points gives a finite étale S₆-torsor Z_ev→V. The deck action is free: a permutation fixing an ordered tuple of six pairwise-distinct points is the identity. This statement concerns the deck group only and says nothing about automorphisms of the marked curve.

5. The open V is S-smooth of pure relative dimension two, and finite étale pullback shows that Z_ev is S-smooth of pure relative dimension two. Conf₆(C/S) is S-smooth of relative dimension six. Since the Abel–Jacobi/Fitting identity makes Z_ev closed in Conf₆, a closed immersion between S-smooth schemes is regular. The relative dimension difference is four, so the conormal is locally free of rank four; the conormal sequence splits locally because Ω_{Z_ev/S} is locally free. This lci conclusion comes from relative smoothness, not from determinantal expected codimension.

6. For each irreducible component S_α, the projective bundle I_α is irreducible, and V_α=V∩I_α is nonempty open and hence irreducible and dense. Thus components of I and V correspond to those of S and have dimension dim(S_α)+2 when finite-dimensional. For a component T of Z_ev, flatness of the finite étale map makes the contraction of its generic point a generic point of V; finiteness then makes T→V_α surjective. Hence dim(T)=dim(V_α)=dim(S_α)+2. The number of such T over V_α is not determined without additional normality and monodromy input.

## Computational hypotheses

None. No finite experiment is used to establish a universal claim.

## Remaining scope

The proof is relative over a reduced scheme base. It does not descend the projective-bundle argument to a stack base, determine moduli inertia, or establish any closed embedding, absolute codimension, Gysin morphism, or Tate statement in M_{6,6}.

claims.justification: Normalization gives L=ω(-D). Clifford leaves h⁰(O(D))∈{2,3}; the equality case is hyperelliptic-composed, which FND-0125 proves has relations splitting O(2)⊕O(7), contradicting balance. Riemann–Roch and Serre duality give the remaining dimensions.
claims.statement: Under (BAL)+(N), every geometric fibre has L≅ω(-D), h⁰(O(D))=2, h⁰(L)=3, and h¹(L)=2; hence the h⁰=4 stratum is empty.

claims.justification: CLM-0094-1 gives constant h⁰=3 and h¹=2. Grauert gives local freeness and base change, and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-4,5 gives the canonical incidence/projective-bundle identification. A projective bundle with irreducible fibre has exactly the inverse images of the base components as its irreducible components.
claims.statement: Over reduced S, the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence is a P²-bundle I≅P_S((π_*L)^∨), and its irreducible components correspond to those of S.

claims.justification: A base point would produce a g²_5 and hence the plane-quintic projection case, excluded from the balanced CE locus by FND-0130. Characteristic-zero Bertini applied to the resulting base-point-free system produces reduced general members.
claims.statement: L is fibrewise base-point-free, and the distinct-support open V is nonempty and dense in every P² fibre.

claims.justification: ATT-0065 gives the Fitting/Picard ideal identity and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6 gives the ordered distinct-support comparison and stack-level torsor. Pairwise distinctness makes the permutation action free.
claims.statement: On Conf₆, Z_ev is scheme-theoretically the ordered incidence over V, and Z_ev→V is a finite étale S₆-torsor with free deck action.

claims.justification: V is an open of a P²-bundle and Z_ev→V is finite étale, while Conf₆→S is smooth of relative dimension six. The closed immersion between S-smooth schemes is regular, with codimension equal to the relative-dimension difference.
claims.statement: Z_ev→S is smooth of pure relative dimension two, and Z_ev↪Conf₆(C/S) is a regular immersion of pure codimension four with locally free rank-four conormal.

claims.justification: For a finite flat map, a minimal prime contracts to a minimal prime; the finite image containing the generic point is the entire target component. Finite morphisms preserve dimension, and V_α is dense open in the P²-bundle over S_α.
claims.statement: Every irreducible component of Z_ev maps finitely and surjectively onto an irreducible component V_α and has dimension dim(S_α)+2 whenever S_α is finite-dimensional.

parsed_artifact.theorem_statement: Let k be a characteristic-zero field and S a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme. Let π:C→S be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected genus-six curves equipped with a finite flat degree-four map γ:C→P¹_S, the standard degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl resolution, fibrewise balanced relations bundle F_s≅O(4)⊕O(5), its canonical filtration with quotient W_5 of degree 16, and the weak relative-canonical normalization (N). Put L=W_5⊗ω_{C/S}^{-1}, let I=Hilb⁶(C/S)×_{Pic⁶(C/S)}S be the Abel–Jacobi incidence over [L], let V=I^{dist} be its distinct-support open, and let Z_ev⊂Conf₆(C/S) be the intrinsic evaluation-failure scheme. Then every geometric fibre has h⁰(L_s)=3 and h¹(L_s)=2; I≅P_S((π_*L)^∨) is a P²-bundle; V is nonempty and dense in every fibre; and Z_ev is scheme-theoretically the ordered incidence over V. The morphism Z_ev→V is a finite étale S₆-torsor with free deck action, Z_ev→S is smooth of pure relative dimension two, and Z_ev↪Conf₆(C/S) is a regular immersion of pure codimension four with locally free conormal of rank four. Irreducible components of I and V correspond to irreducible components of S; every irreducible component of Z_ev maps finitely and surjectively onto one component of V and, over a finite-dimensional component S_α, has dimension dim(S_α)+2. No count of the components of Z_ev is asserted.
